title: Wright Air Development Center anti-gravity research team
place_text: Wright Air Development Center, Dayton, Ohio

tellings.quote: they actually had a team of physics researchers working on anti-gravity at the time at right air Development Center
We know that right airfield had a dedicated team of people working on anti-gravity which included Lewis Whitten father of Ed Whitten who is at Martin Corporation's RA their anti-gravity division
tellings.difference: Names Louis Witten as a team member and ties him to Martin's RIAS anti-gravity division.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the 1950s team of physicists working on anti-gravity at Wright Field / Wright Air Development Center, credited to Josh Goldberg.

as_told.title: Wright Field anti-gravity team including Louis Witten and Martin's RIAS

plain: Michels says that in the 1950s the Wright Air Development Center, an Air Force research base in Dayton, Ohio, had a dedicated team of physicists working on anti-gravity, citing the physicist Joshua Goldberg. In a later episode he adds that the team included Louis Witten, father of the well-known physicist Ed Witten, and ties Louis Witten to an anti-gravity division at the Martin aircraft company that Michels calls RIAS. If true, it would mean the military was studying ways to cancel gravity not long after Roswell.
